rich_summary: Arjuna tells Krishna that the teaching of the supreme spiritual mystery has dispelled his confusion and that he now accepts Krishna’s divine greatness. Yet he longs to directly behold Krishna’s true cosmic form. Krishna grants him "celestial sight" and reveals the Vishvarupa—the universal form containing countless divine aspects, gods, beings, weapons, and ornaments, radiant like a thousand suns. Arjuna sees the entire universe within Krishna’s body and is overwhelmed with awe and terror as he witnesses warriors rushing into the deity’s blazing mouths like moths into fire. Realizing the destructive power behind the vision, Arjuna asks who this fierce form is. Krishna replies that he is Time/Death, the destroyer of worlds, already responsible for the warriors’ fate, and that Arjuna’s role is merely to act as the instrument of a destiny already set.

highlight_spans.why: Krishna’s claim that the universe exists through only a portion of his power establishes the theological scale of the revelation that follows.
Krishna grants Arjuna divine sight and invites him to behold the countless forms and the entire universe within his body—the turning point where the vision begins.
The famous comparison of the divine radiance to the simultaneous rising of a thousand suns captures the overwhelming brilliance of the cosmic form.
Arjuna’s fearful description of beings rushing into Krishna’s blazing mouths like moths to fire conveys the terrifying aspect of divine power.
Krishna’s declaration "I am Death, the destroyer of the worlds" crystallizes the philosophical message: cosmic destruction and destiny are already in motion.

top_scenes.scene_text: Krishna revealing his cosmic form to Arjuna, his body filled with countless faces, arms, weapons, and gods, radiating light like a thousand suns.
Arjuna kneeling in awe before the blazing universal form while the entire universe—stars, gods, and beings—appears within Krishna’s vast body.
Warriors and kings rushing helplessly into the flaming mouths of the cosmic deity like moths flying into a fire.
